newsitem.title: CAMEROON: New Cameroon parliament inaugurated, no boycott.
newsitem.headline: New Cameroon parliament inaugurated, no boycott.

text.p: Cameroon's opposition attended the inaugural session of parliament on Tuesday despite a boycott threat, and vowed to play a full part in proceedings.
The opposition had accused President Paul Biya's Cameroon People's Democratic Rally (RDPC) of fraud after the RDPC won 109 of the 180 seats in the assembly in an election on May 17.
"We are sending our members to parliament to open up a new front there for the struggle for freedom," opposition Social Democratic Front (SDF) leader John Fru Ndi said in Yaounde on Monday.
Diplomats said the opposition parties had dropped plans to boycott the assembly on the advice of Western representatives.
Fru Ndi, who did not seek election, did not attend the inauguration ceremony.
The SDF has 43 seats, the National Union for Democracy and Progress (UNDP) of Bello Bouba Maigari 13, the Cameroon Democratic Union (UDC) five, and three small parties one each.
Results were cancelled in three constituencies accounting for seven seats in all because of what the supreme court described as "severe irregularities and massive fraud".
The SDF and the UNDP called for all results to be scrapped. International observers highlighted problems during polling in what was the second election since the multi-party era began in 1990.
Police dispersed opposition protesters outside the court on June 6 when the final results were announced.
Biya took over from independence president Ahmadou Ahidjo in 1982. He seeks re-election in October.
Fru Ndi lost narrowly to Biya in 1992 in an election which the opposition says was rigged.
